main_text.p: exponant, quod facit Thomas Iacksonus cum Arminianis, nunquam hanc distinctionem intellexisse, vel saltem mentem theologorum nostrorum vaferrime dissimulasse. Nam voluntas approbationis qua talis, non ponit ullam in Deo efficientiam, ne quidem executive: sive ef-fective at vero decretum & voluntas beneplaciti, quamvis sit actus in Deo immanes, non minus quam voluntas approbationis, attamen in executione ponit Deum actu effecturum, quod efficere decrevit, quod voluntas approbans nullo modo ponit, qua talis. Hinc affa-ta ifta ponimus.
1. Deus serió vult, hoc est, amat, approbat, actuque complacentiæ fertur in obedientiam reproborum, quatenus est res bona & sancta, sive actu existat illa obedientia, sive non.
2. Nulla est in Deo voluntas huic contraria, & postquam decrevit ut hæc res, non illa fit moralis obedientia, non potest Deus non serio velle & approbare talem rem.

3. Deum decrevisse aut hortationibus & minis intendisse ab æterno, ut reprobi obedirent & crederent, & interim ipsos reprobasse, & gratiam efficacem, quâ crederent ipsis negasse tali decreto, esset ponere in Deo contradictorias voluntates.
4. Deum velle voluntate signi homines obedire euangelio, & interim iisdem nolle euangelium revelare, est contradictorium.

page.notes: No marginal notes on this page. A thin strip along the right edge is the neighbouring page's edge and is not transcribed. A small stray mark in the left margin beside the line "affa-ta" is not printed text. The catchword "pecca-" is set at the lower right and is recorded as a catchword only. The text "Iacksonus" is copied as printed. Long s is rendered as plain s throughout.
